paper.title_en: Truncated Kiselev environments around black holes: selection rules and a lensing-emission consistency relation
paper.abstract_en: Kiselev-type anisotropic fluids are a standard analytic model of black holes embedded in dark matter or dark energy, but for the dark-sector range of the Kiselev parameter ($w\le 0$), their matter extends to infinity with a divergent ADM mass, so the mass parameters of the metric cannot be tied to the mass a distant observer measures. We remove this obstruction with the truncated Kiselev (TK) geometry, whose dimensionless density $\sigma (r)=4\pi r^{2}\rho$ has a spike-like power-law core of index $\alpha$ and a truncation index $\beta$ that reproduces the NFW-to-Hernquist range of halo fall-offs. We show that $p_{r}=-\rho$ is not an extra assumption but the condition for a single-function metric and for a regular non-degenerate horizon when the fluid reaches it. On $\alpha >0$, $1<\alpha +\beta \le 2$, $\xi \ge 1$, $\sigma _{H}<1/2$ all four energy conditions hold, the ADM mass is finite, the horizon sits at $r=2M$ and the Smarr relation closes. We prove three selection rules: to first order in $\sigma$ the critical curve measures only the Misner-Sharp mass inside the photon sphere, the radiative efficiency only the local density at the ISCO, and the strong-deflection coefficient only $\rho +p_{t}$ at the photon sphere. These yield a mass-independent lensing-emission consistency relation and a dominant-energy bound $\mathfrak {a}\le 15\,\mathfrak {b}$. A first-order slow-rotation extension with a zero-angular-momentum environment leaves the shadow size unchanged at O(J) and relaxes the bound to $\mathfrak {a}\le 15\,\mathfrak {b}+0.238\,J/M^{2}$. Treating M87* and Sgr A* separately, the Sgr A* shadow with independent mass and distance bounds the mass fraction outside the photon sphere to $F_{\textrm{out}}<0.39$ (95%), whereas the M87* bound is limited by its mass systematics.
